newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Regional coffee growers meet in Honduras.
newsitem.headline: Regional coffee growers meet in Honduras.

text.p: Latin American coffee producers met Monday in Honduras in the beginning of a week-long tour to discuss cooperation between coffee growers.

Brazil's former Agriculture Minister, Dejandie Dalpascuale, said at the inauguration that the exchange of information and experiences should allow better quality beans to be marketed on international markets.
He called for participating countries to increase trade to China, Japan, Malaysia and the former Soviet Union.
Representatives from Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Costa Rica, Nicaragua, El Salvador, Guatemala, Panama and Honduras attended the meetings.
After two days in Santa Rosa de Copan, 270 km (165 miles) from the capital of Honduras, the meetings will travel through the region to end in San Jose, Costa Rica.
Organizers said participants intended to exchange experiences and the development of their respective coffee industries.
Honduras Deputy Commerce Minister Julio Gonzales said coffee growing is the principal economic activity in the country, generating more than $350 million per year.
